hero.eyebrow: A safe haven for your photos
hero.h1: Get the photos off your camera. No cable.
hero.lede: {name} brings the photos on your camera safely home to your computer over Wi-Fi: into Apple Photos, a folder or Lightroom. It remembers what it already imported, so next time you only get the new ones.
hero.note: Free and open source · Mac, Windows, Linux

why.h2: Your camera has Wi-Fi. Use it.
why.p1: Most cameras from the last ten years have Wi-Fi, but it was made for a phone app. To get photos onto a computer you're back to cables and card readers, and they are never where you need them.
why.p2: {name} does one thing: it gets your photos from the camera onto your computer, safely and without fuss. It doesn't edit, organize or rate. Your photo app already does that.

steps.d: The same way you would for its phone app. On a Fujifilm camera: Playback, then Wireless Communication.
On your computer, pick the network the camera starts. {name} finds the camera by itself. The first time, confirm on the camera.
Only photos you haven't imported yet are copied, checked, and put where you want them. Or select the ones you want.

how.autosave: Even easier on Fujifilm cameras: with PC AutoSave, the camera sends its new photos to {name} over your home Wi-Fi. No network switching.

features.h2: Everything you need, nothing you don't

items.d: {name} remembers what it imported, even after you delete photos from your computer. No duplicates.
Apple Photos (with an album), any folder, your Pictures folder for Windows Photos, a folder Lightroom watches, or your own Immich server.
On Fujifilm cameras: register the camera once, then choose PC AutoSave on it and it sends its new photos over your home Wi-Fi.
Select photos on the camera and send them, or protect your favorites and import only those.
Every file is checked against what the camera reported and retried if it doesn't match. It warns you before your disk fills up.
Folders by year and date, your own file names, an album per month, and a backup copy to a second drive.
Lives in the menu bar or tray, imports automatically when the camera connects, and tells you when it's done.
No account, no cloud, no tracking. Your photos go from the camera to your computer and nowhere else.

items: Not a photo editor or a Lightroom replacement. It hands your photos to the app you already use.
Not a remote control. It doesn't fire the shutter or change camera settings.
Not a cloud service. There is no account and nothing is uploaded, unless you set up your own Immich server.
It never deletes photos from your camera.

camerasblock.p: Works best today with Fujifilm X and GFX cameras from about 2014 to 2021, the ones that worked with Fujifilm's Camera Remote app. Tested on the X-T20, and on nine more Fujifilm models in an emulator. Canon, Olympus, Ricoh, Sony and Panasonic are experimental.

download.lede: Free, open source (MIT) and signed for each platform. Version {version}.
download.mac_req: macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon and Intel.
download.cli_req: For servers, scripts and a Raspberry Pi: fujictl for macOS, Linux and Windows.

items.a: Fujifilm cameras that worked with the Camera Remote app over Wi-Fi are supported best; {name} replaces that app's photo transfer. Newer Fujifilm models that pair over Bluetooth, like the X-T5 and X-S20, aren't supported yet. Canon, Olympus, Ricoh, Sony and Panasonic are experimental. See the camera list.
Most cameras, Fujifilm included, only send JPEGs over Wi-Fi. That is a limit of the camera, not of {name}. For RAW files you still need a card reader or a cable.

Mostly not. For a full card of RAW files, a card reader is much faster than Wi-Fi. {name} is for the days you don't have one with you, and for sending a few selected photos from the camera to a laptop at an event.
Yes. {name} is open source under the MIT license. There are no ads, subscriptions or in-app purchases.

items.q: Will my computer be offline while importing?
items.a: Yes, while your computer is on the camera's Wi-Fi it can't reach the internet. With PC AutoSave the camera joins your home network instead, so you stay online.

items.q: Does it upload my photos anywhere?
items.a: No. {name} talks to your camera and to the folders or apps you choose. It has no account, no analytics and no servers of its own.

items.q: Does it work with Lightroom, Capture One or Windows Photos?
items.a: Yes. Import into a folder that your photo app watches, or into your Pictures folder for Windows Photos. On a Mac, {name} can also import straight into Apple Photos.

items.q: Does it delete photos from the camera?
items.a: Never. Your card stays exactly as it was. Delete photos on the camera when you're ready.
Canon, Olympus and OM System, Ricoh GR, and older Sony and Panasonic cameras are supported experimentally. If you try one, please tell us whether it worked.

cameras.lede: {name} imports photos over Wi-Fi from the cameras below. A camera that isn't listed may still work: if it can send photos to a phone app over its own Wi-Fi network, try it and let us know.

notes.camera_remote: Same Wi-Fi protocol as the tested models.
notes.bluetooth: These pair over Bluetooth first. Support is planned.
notes.ptpip: Standard PTP/IP over the camera's Wi-Fi.
notes.dlna: Cameras that share photos as a media server on Wi-Fi.
notes.nikon: Needs research with a real camera.

cameras.emulator_note: "Works in the emulator" means {name} passes its tests against vcam, an open-source emulator of that camera's protocol. Real cameras sometimes behave differently.
cameras.report_p: Tell us whether it worked, even if it didn't. Each report moves a camera up this list.

sections.p: {name} collects nothing about you. It has no account, no analytics, no crash reporting and no servers. This website has no cookies, no JavaScript and no tracking.

sections.h: What the app does with your photos
sections.p: {name} connects to your camera over Wi-Fi and copies photos to the places you choose: Apple Photos, a folder on your computer or a backup drive. If you set up an Immich server, it uploads to that server, which you run yourself.
A list of the photos it imported (file name, date and size), so it can skip them next time, and your settings. Both stay on your computer. An Immich API key is stored in the system keychain.
On a Mac, {name} asks for access to Photos to add photos, and for the local network to reach the camera. It only uses that access to add photos and create its album.
This site is hosted by Cloudflare Pages. Cloudflare processes requests to deliver pages and may keep short-lived logs; we don't receive or use them. There are no third-party scripts.
Questions? Open an issue on GitHub.
